prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: []
1: ["Checking Desktop Compatibility", "Verifying overlay permissions and graphics settings for your pet."]
2: ["Make It Official", "Name your pet and sign the official adoption certificate.", "Pet Name", "Sign Certificate"]
3: ["Try Desktop Controls", "Click and drag your pet to practice desktop interactions before completing setup.", "Got It!"]
4: ["How Would You Like to Start?", "Choose a pre-made pet companion or create your own custom companion."]
5: ["Signing into your existing account automatically restores your previously adopted pets and progress."]
6: ["Use clear, well-lit photos facing forward for best custom pet generation accuracy."]
7: ["Setting Up Your Desktop Companion", "Your pet is getting ready! While you wait, test your pet knowledge."]
8: ["Welcome home! Remember: Press Alt+Pet to summon, or right-click your pet to hide or interact."]
9: ["Select Your Starting Path", "Don't worry, you can easily change your pet or adopt additional pets at any time later!"]
